title: Stored-leaf secp256k1 search with explicit scalar push/ACK transport

claims.statement: For uniform unrestricted production secp256k1 ECDLP challenges and fresh algorithm coins, the grouped stored-leaf search in proof.md has success probability at least 0.39 and an upper bound 123.186563709484764 on log2(total expected classical computation in the fixed C=1000 scalar AArch64 instruction normalization). All preprocessing, failed paths, arithmetic, address/control work, transfers, verification and output are included across processors. Peak reserved memory is below 2^138 bytes; there is no free advice or future-target amortization. The estimate retains the reference arithmetic and collision hypotheses, supplies the denominator-cleared selected-X fiber bound in selected-x.md, derives the relay joint events through pointwise ideal labels and ordered-distinct affine-chain kernels, charges the global pair-inverse canonicality exception and its complete capped work, recomputes capacity and persistent-meter losses, and uses the explicit memory-fabric construction, per-processor publication events, and counted scalar services in proof.md and fabric.md. It assumes the stated architectural extensions and platform event/LS64 endpoint conditions, including absence of unrelated/spurious wait events; the specific two-publication control wait is separately charged. The finite experiments establish only their stated source, arithmetic and routing checks, not production execution, RTL synthesis or a production collision law. The runtime archive is lossless in-package evidence with an inspect experiment; current mathematical proofs, generic/initializer assembly and score evaluator remain plain; leaf, route, field, Y-service and chunk-driver sources have exact archive inspection.

experiments.purpose: Recompute exact reference/current success and work; replay current arithmetic, meter, home, bulk, generic, Y, joint-label, selected-X and map/fabric checks with negative controls. Inspect mode exposes exact archived source; optional sections permit deeper bounded replay.
